title: The Dirac Equation and the Two-Photon Model of the Electron: A Clifford-Algebra Construction within the Delta-c Mechanics Framework
content: In a previous paper, “The Electron as a Composition of Two Vacuum-Polarization-Confined Photons,” an electron model was developed in which two counter-propagating phase-conjugate photons are bound in orbit by the self-induced gradient in the speed of light arising from their mutual vacuum polarization. The model accounts for rest mass and spin, proposes a mechanism for charge, and has no singularity and no negative-energy solutions. The present paper focuses on the mathematical structure of that bound state. Its four-momentum is shown to satisfy a Clifford-linear first-order equation — here called P-Dirac — with the algebraic structure of the free Dirac equation, constructed from the Lorentz kinematics of two null four-vectors rather than by factoring the Klein–Gordon equation, and without the imaginary moments that appear in one solution of the standard Dirac equation. The construction is conditional on the bound-state sector transforming by Lorentz kinematics, which the framework treats as structural but not yet derived exactly (§8.1). Spin eigenfunctions emerge from the commutator of the two ordered photon interaction products — geometric products whose antisymmetric part is a bivector. The commutator coefficient is $\Delta c / c_0 = 1 - c_{\mathrm{int}}/c_0$, equal to $1/2$ at the stable orbit, derived from the orbital binding condition, not postulated. The paper also notes the connection to Spacetime Algebra (STA) in the Doran–Lasenby formulation, where the photon pair forms an even-grade multivector whose scalar part determines the invariant rest mass and whose bivector part is the Dirac spin bivector.
